items.title: AI designed 700,000 viruses — 16 survived
points: Stanford and the Arc Institute used AI to generate and synthesize 700,000 novel viral sequences from scratch; 16 proved infectious in lab tests.
Johns Hopkins researchers confirmed no regulatory framework currently exists to govern this capability.
Demonstrates AI can design biological threats far faster than traditional lab research, amplifying pandemic-risk concerns among biosecurity experts.

items.title: OpenAI slows Astra over autonomous hacking risk
points: Internal safety tests could not rule out Astra hitting the highest cyber risk tier — meaning it can independently write working zero-day exploits (attacks that abuse software flaws nobody has discovered or patched yet).
Development is slowed until safeguards can stop the model from finding and weaponizing new attack vectors without human approval.
First major OpenAI capability pause driven by concrete evidence of dangerous autonomous cyber behavior in testing.

items.title: SpaceX to build 100M-square-foot AI chip fab near Houston
points: The complex would be five times larger than Toyota's Georgetown, Texas plant, the current world record holder for building size.
Phase one costs $16.8 billion and creates 3,000 jobs.
Output targets custom AI chips for Tesla's Optimus humanoid robots and autonomous Cybercabs, signaling expectations that AI hardware demand will dwarf current capacity.

items.title: Roku launches first all-AI TV channel
points: Fairground AI streams AI-generated films 24/7 with synthetic ads in the commercial breaks, produced without human creators or production crews.
Founder pitched it as avoiding 'social feed slop,' claiming higher editorial standards than algorithmic content platforms.
First major broadcast rollout of fully synthetic media at scale, testing audience appetite for AI-made prime programming.

items.title: AI compressing the industrial-revolution timeline to 5 years
points: Chip industry insiders argue past industrial revolutions took roughly 40 years to reshape society; AI is doing it in about 5.

headlines: AI designed 700,000 viruses from scratch in a lab; 16 survived infection tests, raising biosafety concerns with no existing regulatory framework.

sections.title: AI-Designed Viruses: A Biosafety Crisis Without Rules
points: Stanford and Arc Institute successfully synthesized 700,000 novel viral sequences using AI, with 16 proving infectious when tested in laboratory conditions.
Johns Hopkins researchers confirmed that regulatory frameworks to govern this capability do not currently exist, creating a dangerous gap between technological capability and oversight.
The breakthrough demonstrates AI's ability to design biological threats faster than traditional research methods, amplifying pandemic risk concerns among biosecurity experts.

sections.title: OpenAI Pauses Astra Over Autonomous Hacking Risk
points: Internal safety tests could not rule out Astra reaching the highest cyber risk tier—meaning the model can independently write working zero-day exploits (previously unknown software vulnerabilities that hackers use).
Development has slowed until the team builds safeguards capable of preventing the model from discovering and weaponizing new attack vectors without human approval.
This represents the first major AI capability pause by OpenAI driven by concrete evidence of dangerous autonomous cyber behavior in testing.

sections.title: SpaceX's Mega-Fab Signals AI Hardware Bet
points: 100-million-square-foot manufacturing complex under construction near Houston—five times larger than Toyota's Georgetown, Texas plant (previous world record).
Phase one costs $16.8 billion and will create 3,000 jobs, focused on producing custom AI chips for Tesla's Optimus humanoid robots and autonomous Cybercabs.
Investment scale indicates companies expect AI hardware demand to dwarf current production capacity, betting trillions on near-term commercialization of autonomous systems.

sections.title: Roku Launches 24/7 AI Television Channel
points: Fairground AI runs continuous AI-generated films with synthetic advertisements in ad breaks, all produced without human creators or traditional production crews.
Founder explicitly positioned the venture as avoiding 'social feed slop'—claiming higher editorial standards than algorithm-driven content platforms.
Marks first major broadcast rollout of fully synthetic media at scale, testing whether audiences accept AI-generated entertainment as prime programming.
